name: D7 Visa (Passive Income)

value.note: passive income only — pensions, rental income, dividends, royalties, interest. +50% of RMMG for a spouse, +30% per child, handled as separate requirements below.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires passive income (pensions, rent, dividends, royalties, or interest) of at least €920/month (100% of the 2026 minimum wage), for the main applicant.
requirements.fix_path: Increase passive income to the required level, or reduce the number of dependants included.

value.note: additional passive income required per accompanying spouse/partner

requirements.blocker_text: Each accompanying spouse or partner adds a further €460/month (50% of RMMG) to the required passive income.

value.note: additional passive income required per accompanying child or dependent

requirements.blocker_text: Each accompanying child or dependent adds a further €276/month (30% of RMMG) to the required passive income.

evidence_required.document: Proof of passive income (pension statements, rental contracts, dividend/interest records)
Portuguese bank account holding approximately 12 months of the required income (consular practice, not a hard statutory figure)

outcome.duration_length: residence permit valid 2 years, renewable for 3 years

sources.title: Portal de Vistos - Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros - subsistence means criterion

notes: FORMULA VALUE, tier-1 confirmed: threshold is explicitly stated by vistos.mne.gov.pt as pegged to RMMG (minimum wage), not IAS — a genuinely high-risk stale-figure area, since Portugal has TWO similarly-named indexed reference figures (RMMG €920/month, IAS €537.13/month) and several tier-3 relocation sites incorrectly imply the D7 threshold is IAS-based. This is arguably the clearest and most consequential counterfeit-figure risk found across all four countries in this dataset — using the wrong reference value would understate the real threshold by nearly half. citizenship_after_months (84) reflects the NEW 7-year naturalisation clock under Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026 (in force 19 May 2026) for CPLP/EU nationals — non-CPLP/EU applicants need 10 years (120 months); this route doesn't restrict by nationality so citizenship_after_months encodes the faster 7-year case with the slower case flagged here rather than forcing an inaccurate single number. MAJOR LIVE POLICY CONTEXT: Portugal's naturalisation clock was DOUBLED from 5 to 7/10 years by a law that took effect during this very research pass (19 May 2026) — any secondary source describing Portugal as a '5-year citizenship' country is now stale, a genuinely dramatic and recent change unlike the more gradual reforms seen in UK/Germany/Netherlands.
